events.title: Terror is declared the order of the day
events.shortBlurb: Pressed by the Paris sections, the National Convention made terror the order of the day, and the machinery of the guillotine turned upon the Church…
body: In the summer of 1793 the Republic stood besieged: royalist rebels held the Vendée, federalist revolts burned in the provinces, and the allied armies pressed the frontiers. On 5 September the Paris sections crowded into the National Convention demanding vengeance on the enemies within, and Bertrand Barère, for the Committee of Public Safety, gave the day its watchword: let terror be placed on the order of the day.

The Convention complied. The Law of Suspects followed on 17 September; the revolutionary calendar swept away the Christian week in October; and in November Notre-Dame itself was rededicated as a Temple of Reason. Across France refractory priests were herded to the guillotine or to the prison-hulks of Rochefort, and the Carmelite nuns of Compiègne would mount the scaffold the following July, singing.

By the reckoning of later historians some sixteen thousand official death sentences were pronounced before the fever broke with Robespierre's fall on 9 Thermidor (27 July 1794), and tens of thousands more perished without judgment. The Church that emerged from the Terror was stripped, scattered, and poorer in everything but its martyrs.
